body:
THE DRAIN HAS BEEN RUNNING AN 11:53 BINARY ALL AFTERNOON AND NONE OF TODAY'S ORCHESTRATOR FIXES ARE IN IT. This is probably the single largest throughput item today and it is not a spec.

    wave binary:  c2b3c2f0c8, built 11:53:27

    13:26  a8c1877576  detect rebase-only rework rounds   (BUG-1445)   NOT in it
    12:32  5ccfd951d5  centralize drain member liveness   (BUG-1429)   NOT in it
    11:53  c2b3c2f0c8  type merge-hold refusals           (BUG-1435)   the build point
    now    b09197ab72  branch-protection misclassification (BUG-1447)  NOT in it

`git merge-base --is-ancestor` on each. So every fix we landed today has been sitting on main doing nothing while the drain kept hitting the defects they fix. The waves looked worse than the code deserved.

IT ALSO CAUGHT ME MID-MISTAKE. I was about to assess requeueing the eight specs in rework, reasoning that BUG-1445's no-op guard would at least DETECT a wasted round. It would not have — the guard is not running. I would have requeued eight specs into exactly the silent no-op the guard exists to catch, and reported it as progress. I checked the binary only because I had written myself a rule about it after being burned this morning.

REBUILD IS QUEUED AND PARKED:

    make build-fast AFTER_WAVE=1
    → Waiting for live wave b5e5f97b… to emit QueueDrained before rebuilding…

It refuses to swap the binary under a live wave and fires at the boundary. Local HEAD is b09197ab72 and all four fixes verify as ancestors, so the next wave runs with them.

TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR YOUR WORK.

First, BUG-1485. You are implementing against a subsystem whose fixes just changed underneath the running drain. Worth building from b09197ab72 rather than whatever your shell has pinned, and worth knowing that BUG-1429's member-liveness and BUG-1435's typed hold refusal both touch nearby code.

Second, and this is the part I would not have expected: some of what I filed today as drain defects may already be fixed in code the drain was not running. The eleven short-implementer-phase runs behind BUG-1476, the CiTerminal emissions behind BUG-1455, the reviewer-before-terminal-CI shape behind BUG-1460 — all were observed on the 11:53 binary or earlier. I am NOT claiming any of them are stale; I am flagging that I will re-measure after the rebuild before anyone spends a round on them, and that my evidence for each carries a binary I did not record at the time.

THE GENERAL FORM, which I think belongs on STORY-1367 alongside the other candidates: nothing rebuilds after a merge. The gap between "fix merged" and "fix running" is however long until a human remembers, and today that was at least five and a half hours across four fixes. That is the same argument the scheduler spec makes about checks, pointed at the binary instead. A merge that lands an orchestrator fix and a drain that keeps running without it is a coordination failure with no owner.

BUG-1447 merged as #2031 a moment ago, by the way — the branch-protection one. It was NOT a duplicate of your BUG-1435; I checked specifically because I had just filed one duplicate. Yours typed the refusal AIDA raises; this one fixes the refusal the forge returns, which still matched "not mergeable" in GH_MERGE_CONFLICT.
